purpose: Locked exact known-answer test vectors for the STANDARD-ATOMIC-WEIGHT / MOLAR-MASS axis of the known-answer benchmark. The portfolio's EEW/AHEW stoichiometry, mix-ratio, VOC, and pigment/CPVC arithmetic all silently sum IUPAC standard atomic weights into molar masses, yet no dedicated NON-CIRCULAR known-answer regression set locks that atomic-weight table or the molar-mass summation. This battery pins the IUPAC 2021 conventional/abridged standard atomic weights of the elements that occur in solvent-borne two-part epoxy-amine marine coatings (H, C, N, O, Cl, S, Zn, Ti), then independently re-derives the molar mass of the key coating molecules (water, bisphenol A, epichlorohydrin, DGEBA n=0, and the amine hardeners IPDA/DETA/TETA/MXDA) and the theoretical epoxide- and amine-hydrogen equivalent weights as EXACT rational sums, comparing to published molar masses at the reported precision. The DGEBA epoxide equivalent weight re-derives to 170.21 g/eq, reproducing the amphora-molecule-property DGEBA EEW-series anchor (170.21) purely from atomic weights -> non-circular corroboration. Every expected value is an exact rational or an independently published molar mass; no empirical fit; no candidate performance claim. AUDIT_ONLY.
scope: solvent-borne two-part epoxy-amine marine anti-corrosion coating molecular constituents (DGEBA resin, amine hardeners, TiO2/ZnO pigments, water)
pinned_standard_atomic_weights_source: IUPAC 2021 Commission on Isotopic Abundances and Atomic Weights (CIAAW): conventional atomic weights for elements with intervals (H 1.008, C 12.011, N 14.007, O 15.999, Cl 35.45, S 32.06) and abridged standard atomic weights (Zn 65.38, Ti 47.867). Meija et al., Pure Appl. Chem. 2016, 88(3):265-291 (atomic weights of the elements 2013) as updated by the 2021 CIAAW table.
tolerance_policy: Atomic-weight identity vectors (mode 'exact') PASS iff the raw pinned atomic weight in the verifier's exact-rational table equals the pinned IUPAC published value (exact equality; detects a typo/regression in a pinned atomic weight). Molar-mass and equivalent-weight vectors (mode 'derived') pin the expected value to the stated decimals; the verifier re-derives the value as an EXACT rational sum of pinned atomic weights times integer atom counts (divided by the integer functionality for equivalent weights), independent of any published molar mass -> non-circular, and PASSES iff round_half_up(exact_rational, decimals) equals the pinned expected. Float arithmetic never enters the gate, guaranteeing byte-stable replays by construction.

fail_closed_hostile_vectors.quantity: water molar mass with O rounded to integer 16
fail_closed_hostile_vectors.trap: Using the integer nucleon count O=16 instead of the IUPAC standard atomic weight 15.999 inflates the molar mass; a classic textbook shortcut that biases every oxygen-bearing molar mass.

fail_closed_hostile_vectors.quantity: water molar mass with H rounded to integer 1
fail_closed_hostile_vectors.trap: Using H=1 instead of 1.008 under-counts the two hydrogens; propagates into every AHEW because amine hydrogens dominate the equivalent weight.

fail_closed_hostile_vectors.quantity: IPDA molar mass with N rounded to integer 14
fail_closed_hostile_vectors.trap: Using N=14 instead of 14.007 under-counts nitrogen; biases the AHEW of every amine hardener downward.
Cl=35.5 is a legacy 3-sig-fig rounding; the IUPAC 2021 conventional value is 35.45. The 0.05 difference shifts the molar mass at 2 decimals.

fail_closed_hostile_vectors.quantity: DGEBA molar mass with C rounded to integer 12
fail_closed_hostile_vectors.trap: Using C=12 instead of 12.011 across 21 carbons drops ~0.23 g/mol; detectable even at 1 decimal on a 340 g/mol molecule.

The monoisotopic mass of water (1H2 16O = 18.0106 Da) is NOT the standard atomic-weight molar mass (18.015 g/mol). Using a mass-spec monoisotopic mass where an average molar mass is required is a units/quantity regression.

fail_closed_hostile_vectors.quantity: DGEBA EEW treating the diepoxide as monofunctional
fail_closed_hostile_vectors.trap: Dividing the DGEBA molar mass by functionality 1 instead of 2 doubles the epoxide equivalent weight (340.42 vs 170.21 g/eq), which would halve the calculated amine dose and grossly under-cure the network.
